questions.stem: What was the woman's first impression of the apartment?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士对这套公寓的第一印象是什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Well, last week when I moved in, the apartment seemed cozy, just the right size for one person. But now it just seems tiny, shabby and solitary. 嗯，上周我刚搬进来时，公寓显得很温馨，对一个人来说大小正合适。但现在它只让人觉得 又小、又破、又孤单。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 时间对照 last week…But now 切出'第一印象'。答案句靠 last week when I moved in 与 But now 形成前后对照：转折前讲的是刚搬进来时（即第一印象），转折后才是现在的感 受。题问 first impression，要取转折前那半句 the apartment seemed cozy, just the right size，别被 But now 后面的负面词带走。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: the apartment seemed cozy, just the right size for one person ↔It was warm and comfortable. cozy=warm and comfortable 的同义概括

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 偷换概念 It was spacious and tranquil. 说'宽敞安静'，但录音只说 just the right size for one person（一人正合适），并非宽敞，tranquil 安静也无对应，属偷换概念。 借用原文：just the right size for one person C) 原词陷阱 shabby and solitary 两词录音确实念到，但出现在 But now it just seems tiny, shabby and solitary——是'现在'的感受，不是题问的'第一印象'，盗用原词答非所问。 借用原文：But now it just seems tiny, shabby and solitary D) 原词陷阱 It was tiny and noisy. 中 tiny 是转折后'现在'的词（now it just seems tiny），noisy 录音 根本没说；既错时间点又有未提及成分。 借用原文：now it just seems tiny

questions.stem: Why does the woman say she is going to sound like an idiot?
questions.stemZh: 为什么这位女士说她听起来会像个傻瓜?
questions.answerText: She misses her roommates she used to complain about.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I'm going to sound like an idiot, because I used to complain to you all the time about how crowded our dormitory room was, and about all the things they did to irritate me… But now I miss them terribly. 我接下来说的会显得很傻，因为我以前老是跟你抱怨宿舍多么拥挤、室友们做的种种让我心 烦的事……可现在我却特别想念他们。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: because 引出原因 + But now 给出反转落点。答案句由 because 直接引出'为何像傻瓜'的 原因，又用 But now I miss them terribly 把态度反转到落点：以前抱怨、现在却想念，这 一反差正是她说自己像傻瓜的缘由。because 与 But now 两个信号叠加锁定此句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I used to complain to you all the time about how crowded our dormitory room was ↔ she used to complain about used to complain 原义保留、对象概括为 roommates But now I miss them terribly ↔She misses her roommates miss them=misses her roommates，代词还原

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 She no longer hates people talking loudly in the dorm. 盗用录音 talking loudly early in the morning 这个原词，但录音说的是'这曾让我心烦'，并没说'不再讨厌'，no longer 是凭空加的极性反转。 借用原文：talking loudly early in the morning C) 原词陷阱 She begins to enjoy the movies she once found irritating. 把录音 watching movies late at night without headphones 和 irritate 拼起来，但录音只说这些事曾让她心烦，从 未说她现在'开始享受电影'，属答非所问。 借用原文：watching movies late at night without headphones D) 原词陷阱 She finds the crowded dorm as cozy as her new apartment. 借用 crowded、cozy 等 词，但录音只说想念室友，从未把'拥挤的宿舍'与'新公寓'做'一样温馨'的比较，属无中生 有。 借用原文：how crowded our dormitory room was

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man when he left the dormitory to live on his own?
questions.stemZh: 当这位男士离开宿舍独自生活时,我们了解到关于他的什么情况?
questions.answerText: He had a similar feeling to the woman's.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: When I got my first place I remember thinking I couldn't wait to live by myself… But then I began missing them and feeling lonely and thinking that our dormitory was like paradise, even though there were six of us guys in one small room. 我有了自己第一个住处时，记得当时心想终于可以一个人住了……可后来我开始想念他们、 感到孤单，觉得我们的宿舍简直像天堂，哪怕当时我们六个大男生挤在一间小屋里。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: But then 后的'想念、孤单'与女方感受平行。男方先说当初迫不及待独居，But then I began missing them and feeling lonely 转折后才是真实感受：想念室友、感到孤单。这 与女方'now I miss them terribly'完全平行，正应了选项'与女方感受相似'。But then 是锁 定真实感受的信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: But then I began missing them and feeling lonely ↔He had a similar feeling to the woman's. 男方'想念+孤单'平行于女方同款感受=similar feeling

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 He found the apartment perfectly furnished. 录音里男方谈的是情绪（想念、孤单）， 从未说他的住处家具完美齐备，属未提及。 B) 过度推断 He had a feeling of despair and frustration. 把男方的 feeling lonely（孤单）夸大成 despair（绝望）、frustration（沮丧），情绪程度被大幅拔高，属过度推断。 借用原文：feeling lonely D) 张冠李戴 He felt the new place was like paradise. 盗用原词 paradise，但录音 thinking that our dormitory was like paradise 说的是'宿舍像天堂'，绝非'新住处像天堂'，把对象张冠李戴 了。 借用原文：thinking that our dormitory was like paradise

questions.stem: What does the man say he can't wait to do?
questions.stemZh: 这位男士说他迫不及待想做什么?
questions.answerText: Go to see the woman's apartment.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: That does sound adorable and I can't wait to see it, and neither can mom and dad. 那听起来确实很可爱，我都等不及要去看看了，爸妈也一样等不及呢。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 意愿标志 I can't wait to see it 直接给出动作。答案句的信号就是 I can't wait to see it， can't wait to 后面的 see it 即男方迫不及待要做的事；it 指上文女方的公寓。题干问 can't wait to do，顺着这个词在原文里一找即得。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I can't wait to see it ↔Go to see the woman's apartment. see it→go to see the apartment，代词还原

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 Make a phone call to his parents. 借用录音 neither can mom and dad 里的父母，但男 方说的是'爸妈也等不及（想看公寓）'，并非'要打电话给父母'，属答非所问。 借用原文：neither can mom and dad C) 未提及 Buy some furniture for the woman. 中 furniture 与女方描述公寓时提到的 sofa、table 沾边，但男方从未说要买家具，属未提及。 D) 张冠李戴 Decorate the woman's apartment. 盗用原词 decorate，但录音 now that I have decorated it 说的是女方已经装饰好了，并非男方迫不及待要去装饰，张冠李戴。 借用原文：now that I have decorated it 1 W: Welcome to our program Book Talk. Our guest today is Frank Jones, a critic of our education system, and the author of a new book, How to Reform Our Universities. W: 欢迎来到我们的节目《书籍对话》。今天的嘉宾是Frank Jones，他是我们教育系统的批评家，也是新 书《如何改革我们的大学》的作者。 2 M: Hello, Susan. M: 你好，Susan。 3 W: Frank, you support radically changing universities in America? W: Frank，你支持从根本上改变美国的大学吗？ 4 M: Yes, I believe that the purpose of higher education is to prepare young people to enter the workforce, and that our current system fails to do this. We're allocating too many resources to disciplines that don't match the needs of employers. M: 是的，我认为高等教育的目的是为年轻人进入职场做准备，而我们现行的系统未能做到这一点。我们 给那些不符合雇主需求的学科分配了太多资源。 5 W: I think your attitude to education is a bit cynical, Frank. Surely the purpose of university is to prepare young people to participate fully in civic life, rather than just to find well-paid jobs. W: 我觉得你对教育的态度有点愤世嫉俗，Frank。大学的目的肯定是让年轻人为充分参与公民生活做准 备，而不仅仅是找到高薪工作。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 6 M: Susan, many young graduates struggle to find any job, let alone a good one. The job market is grim, particularly for students who study the arts. M: Susan，许多年轻毕业生连找份工作都很困难，更别说找份好工作了。就业市场很严峻，特别是对学 习艺术的学生来说。 7 W: I agree that it isn't easy for young people to find work, but you propose closing down all departments that aren't directly related to science and technology. Is that really the solution? W: 我同意年轻人找工作不容易，但你提议关闭所有与科学技术没有直接关系的院系。这真的是解决办 法吗？ 8 M: You're overstating my point. My argument is that we need to use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering. To do that, we need to take money from subjects like literature and music. M: 你夸大了我的观点。我的论点是我们需要把更多预算用在科学和工程这类领域。为了做到这一点，我 们需要从文学和音乐这类学科拿钱。 9 W: But the arts have value. They're an important part of our culture. Studying literature or music or sculpture might not result in a job in that area, but it helps young people to think about the world in a deeper way, which makes them better citizens and makes for a better society. W: 但艺术是有价值的。它们是我们文化的重要组成部分。学习文学、音乐或雕塑可能不会在那个领域找 到工作，但它帮助年轻人以更深刻的方式思考世界，这让他们成为更好的公民，也造就更好的社会。 10 M: I agree that the arts are valuable to society, but it's naive to think that not only the most talented, but all students should study them at university level. The arts are very competitive, and most graduates will end up with a great deal of debt, obtaining a degree that has little value on the job market. M: 我同意艺术对社会有价值，但认为不仅最有天赋的学生，而且所有学生都应该在大学层面学习艺术， 这种想法很天真。艺术竞争非常激烈，大多数毕业生最终会背负大笔债务，获得一个在就业市场上价值不 大的学位。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Our guest today is Frank Jones, a critic of our education system, and the author of a new book, How to Reform Our Universities. 我们今天的嘉宾是 Frank Jones，他是我国教育体制的一位批评者，也是一本新书《如何改 革我们的大学》的作者。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 开场介绍嘉宾句。答案信号是主持人开篇介绍嘉宾的固定句式 Our guest today is Frank Jones，这类“今天的嘉宾是……，他是……的作者”的引荐句，必然交代人物身份，是细节题 的天然落点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: the author of a new book, How to Reform Our Universities ↔He has published a book recently. “新书作者”=“最近出书”

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 录音确说他是 a critic of our education system（教育体制的批评者），A 盗这个 critic 改 成 a literary critic.（文学评论家）——把“批评教育”偷换成“文学评论”，是听到 critic 就想 选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：a critic of our education system B) 张冠李戴 He hosts an educational program.（他主持一档教育节目）说反了人物：主持节目的是女 方 Susan（Welcome to our program Book Talk），男方只是受访嘉宾，把主持人的身份 安到嘉宾头上。 借用原文：Welcome to our program Book Talk C) 过度推断 He has initiated a university reform.（他已发起一场大学改革）盗用了书名里的 reform （How to Reform Our Universities）。他只是写书“主张”改革，并未真的发起改革，把“写 书谈改革”夸成“已发起改革”，属过度推断。 借用原文：How to Reform Our Universities

questions.stem: What does the man believe is the problem with the current American system of higher education?
questions.stemZh: 这位男士认为当前美国高等教育体系存在什么问题?
questions.answerText: It has not prepared young people for the job market.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I believe that the purpose of higher education is to prepare young people to enter the workforce, and that our current system fails to do this. 我认为高等教育的目的是让年轻人为进入职场做好准备，而我们现行的体制没能做到这 一点。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者应答 + fails 否定。答案信号有二：一是这是男方对“你支持激进改革大学吗”的直接 应答（被问者的回答处），二是句中 our current system fails to do this 的否定动词 fails，正点出“制度没做到的事”——即他眼中的问题。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: prepare young people to enter the workforce ↔ It has not prepared young people for the job market. workforce=job market

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 It fails to keep up with the radical changes of society. 借用了原文 radically changing （radically changing universities）的 radical，但男方批的是“没对接就业”，并未说制度 “跟不上社会的剧变”，把原词拼到一个原文没说的归因上。 借用原文：radically changing universities B) 与原文相反 It fails to ensure universities get sufficient resources. 盗用原文 resources（allocating too many resources）。男方说的是资源“分配错地方（过多给了不匹配需求的学科）”，不 是大学“拿不到足够资源”，方向正相反。 借用原文：allocating too many resources to disciplines that don't match the needs of employers D) 与原文相反 It has not fostered the growth of the arts disciplines.（没扶持文科）与男方立场完全相 反：他主张少投文科、多投理工（take money from subjects like literature and music），怎会嫌文科扶持不够。这是把他的对立面安到他头上。 借用原文：take money from subjects like literature and music

questions.stem: How should the education budget be allocated according to the man?
questions.stemZh: 根据这位男士的观点,教育预算应该如何分配?
questions.answerText: More of the budget should go to science and technology.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: My argument is that we need to use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering. To do that, we need to take money from subjects like literature and music. 我的主张是，我们需要把更多预算用在科学和工程这类领域。要做到这一点，我们就得从文 学、音乐这类科目那里抽走经费。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 立论句 My argument is。答案信号是男方亮明主张的标志句 My argument is that we need to use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering——My argument is / we need to 是典型的“建议 / 主张”信号，其后内容即他的真实立场。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering ↔ More of the budget should go to science and technology. “多用预算于”=“更多预算应给”

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 与原文相反 The underfunded music discipline should be prioritized. 盗用原文 music（literature and music）。男方恰恰主张从 music 抽钱（take money from），而非优先扶持 music，方向完全相反。 借用原文：take money from subjects like literature and music C) 张冠李戴 Subdisciplines like sculpture should get more funding. 借用女方后文提到的 sculpture （literature or music or sculpture）。但这是女方为艺术辩护时举的例，男方的主张是给 理工加钱、从文科抽钱，绝不会主张给雕塑这类细分文科加经费，既张冠李戴又方向相反。 借用原文：Studying literature or music or sculpture D) 偷换概念 Literature should get as much funding as engineering. 盗用 literature、engineering 两个原词，却把男方“偏向理工、从文学抽钱”的不均等主张，偷换成“文学与工程经费同 等”。男方要的是倾斜，不是均分。 借用原文：take money from subjects like literature and music

questions.stem: What does the woman say the arts can do?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士认为人文艺术能够做什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Studying literature or music or sculpture might not result in a job in that area, but it helps young people to think about the world in a deeper way, which makes them better citizens and makes for a better society. 学习文学、音乐或雕塑，也许不会带来该领域的工作，但它能帮助年轻人更深入地思考世 界，从而让他们成为更好的公民、造就更好的社会。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 转折 but 后才是真意。答案信号是转折词 but——but it helps young people to think about the world in a deeper way, which makes them better citizens。but 之前的 might not result in a job 是让步铺垫，but 之后才是女方真正要强调的艺术功效。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: which makes them better citizens ↔Cultivate better citizens. “使其成为更好公民”=“培养更好公民”

This week, we will discuss a surprising reason why we might remember some things—anxiety. 在上周的讲座中,我们讨论了人们忘记事情的原因。本周,我们将讨论一个令人惊讶的原因,即为什么我们可 能会记住某些事情——焦虑。 2 Think about something as simple as buying a coffee. That may not seem like an experience that would make a deep impression on your memory, but anxiety could change that. In fact, a new study suggests that people with higher anxiety levels might remember certain information better than people with lower anxiety levels. That's because higher levels of anxiety may make people more susceptible to negative feelings, putting them in a more negative state of mind. That in turn may make them able to better remember some events. 想想像买咖啡这样简单的事情。这似乎不像是一种会给你的记忆留下深刻印象的经历,但焦虑可能会改变这 一点。事实上,一项新研究表明,焦虑水平较高的人可能比焦虑水平较低的人更能记住某些信息。这是因为 较高的焦虑水平可能使人们更容易产生负面情绪,使他们处于更消极的心理状态。这反过来可能使他们能够 更好地记住某些事件。 3 Let's take a closer look at that new study now. In the study, the researchers started by giving 80 undergraduate students an anxiety test. The test measured the participants' anxiety levels over the Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. preceding two weeks. Then, to test memory, the participants were shown a series of neutral words, one at a time. Some of the words were printed on to photos of negative scenes, meaning images that could affect their emotions negatively, such as a photo of a car accident or a cemetery. The rest of the words were printed on to photos of neutral scenes, such as a photo of a lake or trees. Neutral words included words like "table" or "desk" that don't elicit emotion. Later, the participants were asked to think back to the words they were shown earlier, which caused them to reenter either a negative or a neutral mindset. The participants were then presented with another set of neutral words, and their memory of these new words was tested. 现在让我们更仔细地看看这项新研究。在研究中,研究人员首先对80名本科生进行了焦虑测试。该测试测 量了参与者在前两周的焦虑水平。然后,为了测试记忆,参与者被展示了一系列中性词汇,一次一个。其中一 些词汇被印在负面场景的照片上,即可能对他们的情绪产生负面影响的图像,例如车祸或墓地的照片。其余 的词汇被印在中性场景的照片上,例如湖泊或树木的照片。中性词汇包括像"桌子"或"书桌"这样不引发情绪 的词汇。随后,参与者被要求回想他们之前看到的词汇,这使他们重新进入负面或中性的心理状态。然后向 参与者展示另一组中性词汇,并测试他们对这些新词汇的记忆。 4 The researchers found that the new words presented to people in a negative mindset were better remembered by people with higher levels of anxiety than those with lower levels of anxiety. In other words, when highly anxious individuals took in otherwise emotionally neutral information that was presented to them, it became colored by their negative mindset, making them remember the information better. But these same effects were not seen in people with low levels of anxiety. 研究人员发现,呈现给处于负面心理状态的人的新词汇,焦虑水平较高的人比焦虑水平较低的人记得更好。 换句话说,当高度焦虑的个体接收到呈现给他们的原本情感中性的信息时,这些信息被他们的负面心态所影 响,使他们更好地记住了这些信息。但这些相同的效应在低焦虑水平的人身上没有被观察到。 5 Previous studies have found that extreme levels of anxiety, such as those experienced by people diagnosed with an anxiety disorder, can be quite detrimental to memory and cognitive performance. But the highly anxious people in this study represent individuals who are managing their anxiety and for whom anxiety is not a serious problem. 以前的研究发现,极端的焦虑水平,例如被诊断患有焦虑症的人所经历的焦虑,可能对记忆和认知表现相当有 害。但本研究中的高度焦虑者代表的是那些正在控制自己的焦虑且焦虑对他们来说不是严重问题的个体。

It has changed how we communicate with each other, and it has definitely transformed the way we do business with each other. Marketing has also changed in a number of ways. For instance, in the past, consumers had to call a phone number and patiently wait on hold, in order to get the information they wanted. Today, they want the information immediately. They'll go to the company's social media page and post comments and questions, expecting to receive an immediate response. If they don't get their questions answered soon, they'll move on to another company that will answer them quickly. 在过去20年里,互联网逐渐成为我们生活中的主导特征。它改变了我们彼此沟通的方式,也彻底改变了我们 彼此做生意的方式。营销也在许多方面发生了变化。例如,过去消费者必须拨打电话号码并耐心等待,才能 获得他们想要的信息。如今,他们希望立即获得信息。他们会访问公司的社交媒体页面发表评论和提问,期 望立即得到回复。如果他们的问题不能很快得到解答,他们就会转向另一家能够快速回答问题的公司。 2 Marketing departments today need to follow technological development. For example, this year's smartphone is smarter than last year's; self-driving cars are now on the road. Marketers have to do research on which technologies are coming into being. Otherwise, they risk being left behind in the virtual dust. Marketing has also changed due to the importance of video. People don't just want to read text; they want to watch things happening. Companies now have to explore how they can use video on a consistent basis to share information about their businesses. Fortunately, it's extremely easy to shoot something these days. All you need is a smartphone. 如今的营销部门需要跟上技术发展的步伐。例如,今年的智能手机比去年的更智能;自动驾驶汽车现在已经 上路了。营销人员必须研究哪些技术正在兴起。否则,他们就有被抛在虚拟尘埃中的风险。营销也因视频的 重要性而发生了变化。人们不只是想阅读文字;他们想看到事情的发生。公司现在必须探索如何持续使用视 频来分享关于其业务的信息。幸运的是,如今拍摄视频极其容易。你所需要的只是一部智能手机。 3 But what's the result of all this? Shorter attention spans. We aren't the same people that we were 20 years ago. Not only have we grown accustomed to getting the information we want instantaneously, our attention spans are much shorter. If something doesn't capture our attention within a few seconds, we're on to the next piece of content. Marketers need to figure out ways to speak directly to the customers' emotions, and they need to figure out how to do that as quickly as possible. Once people are emotionally engaged, they'll stick with you. 但这一切的结果是什么呢?注意力持续时间更短了。我们已经不再是20年前的那些人了。我们不仅习惯了 即时获取想要的信息,我们的注意力持续时间也变得更短了。如果某样东西不能在几秒钟内吸引我们的注意 力,我们就会转向下一条内容。营销人员需要找出直接触动客户情感的方法,而且他们需要尽可能快地找出 如何做到这一点。一旦人们在情感上被吸引,他们就会持续关注你。 4 If marketing has changed this much in the past 20 years, imagine what the next 20 years will bring. In a recent survey, only 9% of marketers could say with confidence that their marketing efforts were actually working. Their confidence is being shaken, because the rules of the game change every year. That's why it's important for marketers to pay attention to the latest technological developments and consider collaborating with technological innovators. That way, they'll be moving at the same pace as the tech industry. 如果营销在过去20年里已经发生了如此大的变化,想象一下未来20年将会带来什么。在最近的一项调查中, 只有9%的营销人员能够自信地说他们的营销努力确实有效。他们的信心正在动摇,因为游戏规则每年都在 变化。这就是为什么营销人员关注最新技术发展并考虑与技术创新者合作很重要。这样,他们就能与科技行 业保持同步。

questions.stem: What is likely to happen to larger parts of our daily life as machine learning algorithms improve?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: As machine learning algorithms improve and as they train on more extensive data sets, larger parts of everyday life are likely to become utterly predictable. 随着机器学习算法的改进、以及在更大数据集上的训练，日常生活越来越大的部分将变得完 全可被预测。

questions.stem: What do we learn about phonics in many American classrooms?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: What do we learn about phonics in many American classrooms? 用 What do we learn about 直接索取关于某物的客观信息，对应原文应有一句明确表态。

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: 结构平铺直叙：What do we learn about phonics in many American classrooms? 是一 个简单的特殊疑问句，about phonics 是 learn 的宾语补足部分，in many American classrooms 是地点状语，无陷阱。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: But in many classrooms, this can be a dirty word. So much so that some teachers have had to sneak phonics teaching materials into the classroom. 但在许多课堂里，它（拼读法）几乎成了一个令人嫌弃的词。以至于一些老师不得不偷偷把 拼读法教材带进教室。

analysis.label: 选项

analysis.label: 判型

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: What has America been witnessing for decades? 主干 America has been witnessing what，for decades 是持续性时间状语，与现在完成进行时呼应。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: America is stuck in a debate about teaching children to read that has been going on for decades. 美国陷入了一场关于如何教孩子阅读的争论，这场争论已经持续了几十年。

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) 偷换概念 An obsession with innovating teaching methodologies of reading. 把核心从 "争 论" 偷换成 "对创新阅读教学法的痴迷"，原文谈的是两派持续对立而非痴迷创新。 B) ✓ 正确 a debate about teaching children to read ↔ An enduring debate over the approach to teaching children to read. has been going on for decades ↔enduring B 项把定位句里 "持续数十年" + "关于教孩子阅读的争论" 两个核心元素分别压缩为 enduring + debate over the approach to teaching children to read，与预判精准 对应。 C) 偷换概念 An increasing concern with many children's inadequacy in literacy. 把对象换成 "对 许多孩子识字不足的担忧"，原文 P2 提到识字率低只是后果数据，并不是 "美国数十年 来一直在见证" 的主体。 D) 与原文相反 An ever-forceful advocacy of a combined method for teaching reading. 说 "对组 合法越来越有力的倡导"，但原文明确通过 Tenette Smith 说 This combination of methods is ineffective，与选项方向相反。 52. analysis.label: 判型

analysis.label: 拆句
analysis.text: Why does Tenette Smith think a combination of teaching methods is ineffective? Why 引导，think 后接 that 从句（that 省略），从句主语是 a combination of teaching methods，谓语 is ineffective，结构清晰。

analysis.text: "You can't sprinkle in a little phonics," says Tenette Smith, executive director of elementary education and reading at Mississippi's education department. "It has to be systematic and explicitly taught." "你不能只是零星地撒点拼读法进去"，密西西比州教育部基础教育与阅读执行主任 Tenette Smith 说，"它必须被系统、明确地教授。" 53. Why does Tenette Smith think a combination of teaching methods is ineffective? A) Elementary schoolchildren will be frustrated when taught with several methods combined. B) Phonics has to be systematically applied and clearly taught to achieve the desired effect. C) Sprinkling in a little phonics deters the progress of even adequately motivated children. D) Balanced literacy fails to sustain children's interest in developing a good reading habit.

You can't sprinkle in a little phonics ↔Phonics has to be systematically applied 选项 Phonics has to be systematically applied and clearly taught to achieve the desired effect. 把 Tenette Smith 引号里的两条要求 systematic + explicitly taught 完整保留，与预判一致。 C) 过度推断 Sprinkling in a little phonics deters the progress of even adequately motivated children. 把原文的 "不能零星撒拼读法" 错误延伸为 "零星撒拼读法会阻碍连足够有动力 的孩子的进步"，文中并未谈到 "motivated children" 或被 "deter" 这一具体后果。 D) 偷换概念 Balanced literacy fails to sustain children's interest in developing a good reading habit. 把无效的原因换成 "无法维持孩子对培养良好阅读习惯的兴趣"，原文 Tenette Smith 完全没谈兴趣/习惯。 作者说 Mississippi 州的成功归因于什么？ A) 召集全国阅读委员会来综合研究证据。 B) 对流畅性和理解力都给予充分重视。 C) 采用有科学依据的阅读教学方法。 D) 获得国会支持以升级教学方法。

questions.stem: What have advances in statistics and brain imaging proved ineffective?

A) Gratitude may be more beneficial than we commonly suppose. One recent study asked participants to write a note of thanks to someone and then estimate how surprised and happy the recipient would feel—an impact that they consistently underestimated. Another study assessed the health benefits of writing thank-you notes. The researchers found that writing as few as three weekly thank-you notes over the course of three weeks improved life satisfaction, increased happy feelings and reduced symptoms of depression.
B) While this research into gratitude is relatively new, the principles involved are anything but. Students of mine in a political philosophy course at Indiana University are reading Daniel Defoe's 300-year- old Robinson Crusoe, often regarded as the first novel published in English. Left alone on an unknown island with no apparent prospect of rescue or escape, Crusoe has much to lament(悲叹). But instead of giving in to despair, he makes a list of things for which he is grateful, including the fact that he is the sole survivor from the shipwreck(海难) and has been able to salvage many useful items from the wreckage.
C) Defoe's masterpiece, which is often ranked as one of the world's greatest novels, provides a portrait of gratitude in action that is as timely and relevant today as it has ever been. It is also one with which contemporary psychology and medicine are just beginning to catch up. Simply put, for most of us, it is far more helpful to focus on the things in life for which we can express gratitude than those that incline us toward resentment and lamentation.
D) When we focus on the things we regret, such as failed relationships, family disputes, and setbacks in career and finance, we tend to become more regretful. Conversely, when we focus on the things we are grateful for, a greater sense of happiness tends to spread through our lives. And while no one would argue for cultivating a false sense of blessedness, there is mounting evidence that counting our blessings is one of the best habits we can develop to promote mental and physical health.
E) Gratitude has long enjoyed a privileged position in many of the world's cultural traditions. For example, some ancient Western philosophers counsel gratitude that is both enduring and complete, and some Eastern thinkers portray it as not merely an attitude but a virtue to be put into practice.
F) Recent scientific studies support these ancient teachings. Individuals who regularly engage in gratitude exercises, such as counting their blessings or expressing gratitude to others, exhibit increased satisfaction with relationships and fewer symptoms of physical illness. And the benefits are not only psychological and physical. They may also be moral—those who practice gratitude also view their lives less materialistically and suffer from less envy.
G) There are multiple explanations for such benefits of gratefulness. One is the fact that expressing gratitude encourages others to continue being generous, thus promoting a virtuous cycle of goodness in relationships. Similarly, grateful people may be more likely to reciprocate( 回报) with acts of kindness of their own. Broadly speaking, a community in which people feel grateful to one another is likely to be a more pleasant place to live than one characterized by mutual suspicion and resentment. The beneficial effects of gratitude may extend even further. For example, when many people feel good about what someone else has done for them, they experience a sense of being lifted up, with a corresponding enhancement of their regard for humanity. Some are inspired to attempt to become better people themselves, doing more to help bring out the best in others and bringing more goodness into the world around them.
H) Gratitude also tends to strengthen a sense of connection with others. When people want to do good things that inspire gratitude, the level of dedication in relationships tends to grow and relationships seem to last longer. And when people feel more connected, they are more likely to choose to spend their time with one another and demonstrate their feelings of affection in daily acts.
I) Of course, acts of kindness can also foster discomfort. For example, if people feel they are not worthy of kindness or suspect that some ulterior(别有用心的) motive lies behind it, the benefits of gratitude will not be realized. Likewise, receiving a kindness can give rise to a sense of indebtedness, leaving beneficiaries feeling that they must now pay back whatever good they have received. Gratitude can flourish only if people are secure enough in themselves and sufficiently trusting to allow it to do so. Another obstacle to gratitude is often called a sense of entitlement. Instead of experiencing a benefaction(善行) as a good turn, people sometimes regard it as a mere payment of what they are owed, for which no one deserves any moral credit.

One is simply spending time on a regular basis thinking about someone who has made a difference, or perhaps writing a thank-you note or expressing such gratitude in person. Others are found in ancient religious disciplines, such as reflecting on benefactions received from another person or actually praying for the health and happiness of a benefactor. In addition to benefactions received, it is also possible to focus on opportunities to do good oneself, whether those acted on in the past or hoped for in the future. Some people are most grateful not for what others have done for them but for chances they enjoyed to help others. In regularly reflecting on the things in his life he is grateful for, Defoe's Crusoe believes that he becomes a far better person than he would have been had he remained in the society from which he originally set out on his voyage.
K) Reflecting on generosity and gratitude, the great basketball coach John Wooden once offered two counsels to his players and students. First, he said, "It is impossible to have a perfect day unless you have done something for someone who will never be able to repay you." In saying this, Wooden sought to promote purely generous acts, as opposed to those performed with an expectation of reward. Second, he said, "Give thanks for your blessings every day."
L) Some faith traditions incorporate such practices into the rhythm of daily life. For example, adherents of some religions offer prayers of thanksgiving every morning before rising and every night before lying down to sleep. Others offer thanks throughout the day, such as before meals. Other less frequent special events, such as births, deaths and marriages, may also be heralded by such prayers.
M) When Defoe depicted Robinson Crusoe making thanksgiving a daily part of his island life, he was anticipating findings in social science and medicine that would not appear for hundreds of years. Yet he was also reflecting the wisdom of religious and philosophical traditions that extend back thousands of years. Gratitude is one of the healthiest and most nourishing of all states of mind, and those who adopt it as a habit are enriching not only their own lives but also the lives of those around them. 36. It does us far more good to focus on things we can be grateful for than what makes us sad and resentful.

P1 Technology is never a neutral tool for achieving human ends. Technological innovations reshape people as they use these innovations to control their environment. Artificial intelligence, for example, is altering humanity.

P2 While the term AI conjures up anxieties about killer robots or catastrophic levels of unemployment, there are other, deeper implications. As AI increasingly shapes the human experience, how does this change what it means to be human? Central to the problem is a person's capacity to make choices, particularly judgments that have moral implications.

P3 Aristotle argued that the capacity for making practical judgments depends on regularly making them—on habit and practice. We see the emergence of machines as substitute judges in a variety of Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage. everyday contexts as a potential threat to people learning how to effectively exercise judgment themselves.

P4 In the workplace, managers routinely make decisions about who to hire or fire and which loan to approve, to name a few. These are areas where algorithmic(算法的) prescription is replacing human judgment, and so people who might have had the chance to develop practical judgment in these areas no longer will.

P5 Recommendation engines, which are increasingly prevalent intermediaries in people's consumption of culture, may serve to constrain choice and minimize luck. By presenting consumers with algorithmically selected choices of what to watch, read, stream and visit next, companies are replacing human taste with machine taste. In one sense, this is helpful. After all, machines can survey a wider range of choices than any individual is likely to have the time or energy to do on their own.

P6 At the same time, though, this selection is optimizing for what people are likely to prefer based on what they've preferred in the past. We think there is some risk that people's options will be constrained by their past in a new and unanticipated way.

P7 As machine learning algorithms improve and as they train on more extensive data sets, larger parts of everyday life are likely to become utterly predictable. The predictions are going to get better and better, and they will ultimately make common experiences more efficient and pleasant.

P8 Algorithms could soon—if they don't already—have a better idea about which show you'd like to watch next and which job candidate you should hire than you do. One day, humans may even find a way for machines to make these decisions without some of the biases that humans typically display.

P9 But to the extent that unpredictability is part of how people understand themselves and part of what people like about themselves, humanity is in the process of losing something significant. As they become more and more predictable, the creatures inhabiting the increasingly AI-mediated world will become less and less like us.

P1 Phonics, which involves sounding out words syllable(音节) by syllable, is the best way to teach children to read. But in many classrooms, this can be a dirty word. So much so that some teachers have had to sneak phonics teaching materials into the classroom. Most American children are taught to read in a way that study after study has found to be wrong.

P2 The consequences of this are striking. Less than half of all American adults were proficient readers in 2017. American fourth graders rank 15th on the Progress in International Literacy Study, an international exam.

P3 America is stuck in a debate about teaching children to read that has been going on for decades. Some advocate teaching symbol-sound relationships (the sound k can be spelled as c, k, ck, or ch), known as phonics. Others support an immersive approach (using pictures of a cat to learn the word cat), known as "whole language". Most teachers today, almost three out of four according to a survey by the Ed Week Research Centre in 2019, use a mix called "balanced literacy". This combination of methods is ineffective. "You can't sprinkle in a little phonics," says Tenette Smith, executive director of elementary Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage. education and reading at Mississippi's education department. "It has to be systematic and explicitly taught."

P4 Mississippi, often behind in social policy, has set an example here. In a state once notorious for its low reading scores, the Mississippi state legislature passed new literacy standards in 2013. Since then Mississippi has seen remarkable gains. Its fourth graders have moved from 49th (out of 50 states) to 29th on the National Assessment of Educational Progress, a nationwide exam. In 2019 it was the only state to improve its scores. For the first time since measurement began, Mississippi's pupils are now average readers, a remarkable achievement in such a poor state.

P5 Mississippi's success is attributed to implementing reading methods supported by a body of research known as the science of reading. In 1997 Congress requested the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development and the Department of Education to convene a National Reading Panel to end the "reading wars" and synthesize the evidence. The panel found that phonics, along with explicit instruction in phonemic(音位的) awareness, fluency and comprehension, worked best.

P6 Yet over two decades on, "balanced literacy" is still being taught in classrooms. But advances in statistics and brain imaging have disproved the whole-language method. To the teacher who is a proficient reader, literacy seems like a natural process that requires educated guessing, rather than the deliberate process emphasized by phonics. Teachers can imagine that they learned to read through osmosis(潜移默化) when they were children. Without proper training, they bring this to classrooms.

writing.model: Today there is a growing awareness that mental well-being needs to be given as much attention as physical health. For too long, we have measured a person's health only by the body, ignoring the mind that quietly suffers behind a healthy-looking face. Yet a troubled mind can be just as disabling as a broken leg, which is why the two deserve equal care. My own experience convinces me of this. During my sophomore year, a close friend kept a perfect exercise routine but slid into deep anxiety before exams. He looked strong, so no one noticed until his grades and sleep collapsed. Only after he sought counseling did he truly recover. His story shows that neglecting the mind can undo all the benefits of a fit body. Therefore, we should treat mental and physical health as two wheels of the same cart. Schools and workplaces ought to offer counseling as readily as gyms, and each of us should learn to talk about our feelings without shame. When the mind is cared for as much as the body, a person can be genuinely, fully healthy.

translation.reference: In recent years, more and more Chinese cultural products have been entering the global market and winning increasing favor among overseas consumers. With the rapid development of China's foreign cultural trade, the export value of Chinese cultural products has ranked among the world's top for many years, forming a number of internationally influential cultural enterprises, products and brands. Data show that the overseas sales of China's publications, film and TV works, online literature and animation works have been rising year by year. The Chinese government has introduced a series of policies to encourage and support more fine cultural products with Chinese elements to go global, expand their overseas market share, and further enhance the global influence of Chinese culture.

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 以「文化产品」作主语的主谓结构（主语策略：原句主语） 中文主语明确就是 越来越多的中国文化产品，核心动作是「走向全球市场」，所以主干定为 more and more Chinese cultural products + are entering / reaching + the global market。主语直 接沿用原句主语，不必转被动。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 后半句「日益受青睐」降级为并列谓语或现在分词 本句有两个动作：「走向全球市场」和 日益受到海外消费者的青睐。只留「走向」作主干谓语，把 「受青睐」处理成并列谓语用 and 连接（…are entering the global market and winning increasing favor among overseas consumers），或降级成现在分词状语 winning increasing favor…。「日益」译 increasingly／increasing 表程度递增。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时；「近年来…越来越多」强调正在持续的趋势，可用现在进行时 are entering 凸显「正在不断地」，与 越来越多 的递增义吻合。 单复数 products 用复数（泛指一类产品，且前有 more and more）；consumers 用复数（海外消费者 是一群人）。 搭配 「受青睐」译 win favor / be favored / be popular among；among overseas consumers 用 among 接复数人群，不要用 in。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: In recent years, more and more Chinese cultural products have been entering the global market and winning increasing favor among overseas consumers. 2. 随着中国对外文化贸易的快速发展,中国文化产品出口额已持续多年位居世界前列,形成了一批 具有国际影响力的文化企业、产品和品牌。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 以「出口额」作主语的主谓结构（主语策略：原句主语） 「随着…」是状语，不是主干。真正的主干是 中国文化产品出口额已持续多年位居世界前列：主语 the export value of Chinese cultural products，谓语 has ranked among the world's top，构 成主谓。后面「形成了一批…企业、产品和品牌」另起一个动作，作并列或结果处理。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「随着」译介词短语状语，「形成了」降级为现在分词结果状语 随着中国对外文化贸易的快速发展 译成 With the rapid development of China's foreign cultural trade，作句首状语。主句讲出口额位居前列。最后 形成了一批具有国际影响力的文化企 业、产品和品牌 是前面发展带来的结果，降级成现在分词 forming a number of internationally influential cultural enterprises, products and brands，挂在主句后，避免用 and 平铺成第三个 散句。「具有国际影响力的」用形容词 internationally influential 作前置定语。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 已持续多年位居世界前列 强调「持续多年至今」，用现在完成时 has ranked，不能用一般过去时 （过去时会切断与现在的联系）。 主谓一致 主语 the export value 是不可数单数概念，谓语用 has ranked（第三人称单数），不是 have。 单复数 「一批…企业、产品和品牌」三个名词都用复数 enterprises, products and brands；a number of 后必须接复数。 搭配 「位居世界前列」译 rank among the world's top / be among the world leaders；「具有国际 影响力」译 internationally influential 或 with international influence。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: With the rapid development of China's foreign cultural trade, the export value of Chinese cultural products has ranked among the world's top for many years, forming a number of internationally influential cultural enterprises, products and brands. 3. 数据显示,中国的出版物、影视作品、网络文学与动漫作品等在海外的销售量连年攀升。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 以「销售量」作主语、Data show 引导宾语从句（主语策略：原句主语） 数据显示 译成 Data show that… 引出一个宾语从句。从句的主干是 …销售量连年攀升：主语 the overseas sales of China's publications, film and TV works, online literature and animation works，谓语 have been rising year by year。主语沿用原句的「销售量」。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 并列宾语用顿号转逗号加and，「在海外」作定语 中文并列项 出版物、影视作品、网络文学与动漫作品等 在英文里用 A, B, C and D 排列（顿号 逗 号，最后用 and 连接），「等」可用 and so on 或 such as 引导、或直接省略。「在海外」修饰 销售量，译成 overseas（形容词前置）或 in overseas markets（介词短语后置定语）。本句结构 清楚，主要工作是排好并列项和定语。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 连年攀升 表示「逐年持续上升至今」，用现在完成进行时 have been rising 最贴切（强调持续过 程），也可用现在完成时 have risen / have kept rising。 主谓一致 从句主语是 the overseas sales（复数概念，多类产品的销售量），谓语用 have been rising，不 是 has。 单复数 并列各项酌情用复数：publications、works 用复数；online literature 不可数不加 s。 搭配 「连年攀升」译 rise year by year / keep rising over the years；「销售量」译 sales（复数表销 售额／销量）。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Data show that the overseas sales of China's publications, film and TV works, online literature and animation works have been rising year by year. 4. 中国政府出台了一系列政策鼓励和支持更多具有中国元素的优秀文化产品走出国门,扩大海外 市场份额,进一步提升中国文化的世界影响力。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 以「中国政府」作主语、「出台政策」为主干（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是 中国政府（the Chinese government），核心动作是 出台了一系列政策（has introduced / issued a series of policies）。后面「鼓励和支持…走出国门，扩大…份额，提升… 影响力」都是政策的目的，挂在主干之后处理。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「鼓励支持」用to引导目的，三个连动作目的状语 鼓励和支持更多具有中国元素的优秀文化产品走出国门 用不定式 to encourage and support… 表 政策目的；其中「文化产品走出国门」用宾语补足语结构 support more fine cultural products with Chinese elements to go global。后面 扩大海外市场份额,进一步提升中国文化的世界影响力 是连续的目的，并列成 to expand their overseas market share and further enhance the global influence of Chinese culture。「具有中国元素的」用 with Chinese elements 作后置定 语，别前置堆砌。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 出台了一系列政策 是已完成且影响延续至今的动作，用现在完成时 has introduced / has rolled out；目的状语里的不定式不受时态影响，用原形 to encourage。 主谓一致 主语 the Chinese government 是单数，谓语用 has introduced（第三人称单数）。 单复数 policies 用复数（一系列政策）；products 复数；elements 复数（中国元素，多种）。 搭配 「走出国门」译 go global / reach overseas markets；「扩大市场份额」译 expand market share；「提升影响力」译 enhance / boost the influence；「一系列」译 a series of / a set of。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The Chinese government has introduced a series of policies to encourage and support more fine cultural products with Chinese elements to go global, expand their overseas market share, and further enhance the global influence of Chinese culture. 英语六级 2023年6月·第1套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
